## Now Accepting Applications. Exclusively for AOPA Members.

Two annual scholarship periods to help our members achieve their aviation goals! Thanks to generous donor support, we award over $1 million each year to help AOPA members take the next step in their aviation journey, whether that’s pursuing primary flight training, earning advanced ratings and certificates, or building a career through pathways like aviation maintenance.

[APPLY NOW](https://aopafoundation.secure-platform.com/site)

#### Key Details

- **Fall Application Period**: October 1–December 31, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Fall period applicants will be notified of award decisions by April 15)
- **Spring Application Period:** April 1 - June 30, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Spring period applicants will be notified of award decisions by September 15).
- **Eligibility:** Open to current AOPA members who are residents of the United States & District of Columbia, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Not a member? [Click]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]) here to see our membership options. High School students qualify for a [free membership]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]).
- **Award Amounts:**
  - Numerous scholarship opportunities ranging from $250 to $14,000 (amounts may vary depending on donor funding)

#### How It Works

1. **Sign In:** Create an account in our application system (your AOPA login won’t work here).
2. **Complete the General Application:** With just one application, you’ll automatically be matched to all scholarships you’re eligible for. The total number and value of scholarships will be determined by donor funding, which may be finalized just before the awards are announced.
3. **Upload Required Documents:** Transcript, references, and other materials must be submitted before the deadline.
4. **Submit On Time:** Late or incomplete applications will not be accepted.
5. **Didn’t Get Selected?** You're welcome to resubmit your application for the next scholarship application period.

#### If You’re Selected

- Scholarship awardees will be notified by April 15 for the fall application period and by September 15 for the spring application period. Please use an address you check regularly.
- Scholarship funds are provided via a prepaid expense card.
- Scholarship funds expire 12 months after the award date for flight training scholarships and 24 months after the award date for aviation maintenance scholarships.

evidence.excerpt:
## Now Accepting Applications. Exclusively for AOPA Members.

Two annual scholarship periods to help our members achieve their aviation goals! Thanks to generous donor support, we award over $1 million each year to help AOPA members take the next step in their aviation journey, whether that’s pursuing primary flight training, earning advanced ratings and certificates, or building a career through pathways like aviation maintenance.

[APPLY NOW](https://aopafoundation.secure-platform.com/site)

#### Key Details

- **Fall Application Period**: October 1–December 31, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Fall period applicants will be notified of award decisions by April 15)
- **Spring Application Period:** April 1 - June 30, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Spring period applicants will be notified of award decisions by September 15).
- **Eligibility:** Open to current AOPA members who are residents of the United States & District of Columbia, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Not a member? [Click]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]) here to see our membership options. High School students qualify for a [free membership]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]).
- **Award Amounts:**
  - Numerous scholarship opportunities ranging from $250 to $14,000 (amounts may vary depending on donor funding)

#### How It Works

1. **Sign In:** Create an account in our application system (your AOPA login won’t work here).
2. **Complete the General Application:** With just one application, you’ll automatically be matched to all scholarships you’re eligible for. The total number and value of scholarships will be determined by donor funding, which may be finalized just before the awards are announced.
3. **Upload Required Documents:** Transcript, references, and other materials must be submitted before the deadline.
4. **Submit On Time:** Late or incomplete applications will not be accepted.
5. **Didn’t Get Selected?** You're welcome to resubmit your application for the next scholarship application period.

#### If You’re Selected

- Scholarship awardees will be notified by April 15 for the fall application period and by September 15 for the spring application period. Please use an address you check regularly.
- Scholarship funds are provided via a prepaid expense card.
- Scholarship funds expire 12 months after the award date for flight training scholarships and 24 months after the award date for aviation maintenance scholarships.

evidence.excerpt:
## Now Accepting Applications. Exclusively for AOPA Members.

Two annual scholarship periods to help our members achieve their aviation goals! Thanks to generous donor support, we award over $1 million each year to help AOPA members take the next step in their aviation journey, whether that’s pursuing primary flight training, earning advanced ratings and certificates, or building a career through pathways like aviation maintenance.

[APPLY NOW](https://aopafoundation.secure-platform.com/site)

#### Key Details

- **Fall Application Period**: October 1–December 31, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Fall period applicants will be notified of award decisions by April 15)
- **Spring Application Period:** April 1 - June 30, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Spring period applicants will be notified of award decisions by September 15).
- **Eligibility:** Open to current AOPA members who are residents of the United States & District of Columbia, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Not a member? [Click]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]) here to see our membership options. High School students qualify for a [free membership]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]).
- **Award Amounts:**
  - Numerous scholarship opportunities ranging from $250 to $14,000 (amounts may vary depending on donor funding)

#### How It Works

1. **Sign In:** Create an account in our application system (your AOPA login won’t work here).
2. **Complete the General Application:** With just one application, you’ll automatically be matched to all scholarships you’re eligible for. The total number and value of scholarships will be determined by donor funding, which may be finalized just before the awards are announced.
3. **Upload Required Documents:** Transcript, references, and other materials must be submitted before the deadline.
4. **Submit On Time:** Late or incomplete applications will not be accepted.
5. **Didn’t Get Selected?** You're welcome to resubmit your application for the next scholarship application period.

#### If You’re Selected

- Scholarship awardees will be notified by April 15 for the fall application period and by September 15 for the spring application period. Please use an address you check regularly.
- Scholarship funds are provided via a prepaid expense card.
- Scholarship funds expire 12 months after the award date for flight training scholarships and 24 months after the award date for aviation maintenance scholarships.

## Now Accepting Applications. Exclusively for AOPA Members.

Two annual scholarship periods to help our members achieve their aviation goals! Thanks to generous donor support, we award over $1 million each year to help AOPA members take the next step in their aviation journey, whether that’s pursuing primary flight training, earning advanced ratings and certificates, or building a career through pathways like aviation maintenance.

[APPLY NOW](https://aopafoundation.secure-platform.com/site)

#### Key Details

- **Fall Application Period**: October 1–December 31, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Fall period applicants will be notified of award decisions by April 15)
- **Spring Application Period:** April 1 - June 30, 11:59 p.m. ET (all Spring period applicants will be notified of award decisions by September 15).
- **Eligibility:** Open to current AOPA members who are residents of the United States & District of Columbia, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Not a member? [Click]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]) here to see our membership options. High School students qualify for a [free membership]([query-bearing membership locator withheld]).
- **Award Amounts:**
  - Numerous scholarship opportunities ranging from $250 to $14,000 (amounts may vary depending on donor funding)

#### How It Works

1. **Sign In:** Create an account in our application system (your AOPA login won’t work here).
2. **Complete the General Application:** With just one application, you’ll automatically be matched to all scholarships you’re eligible for. The total number and value of scholarships will be determined by donor funding, which may be finalized just before the awards are announced.
3. **Upload Required Documents:** Transcript, references, and other materials must be submitted before the deadline.
4. **Submit On Time:** Late or incomplete applications will not be accepted.
5. **Didn’t Get Selected?** You're welcome to resubmit your application for the next scholarship application period.

#### If You’re Selected

- Scholarship awardees will be notified by April 15 for the fall application period and by September 15 for the spring application period. Please use an address you check regularly.
- Scholarship funds are provided via a prepaid expense card.
- Scholarship funds expire 12 months after the award date for flight training scholarships and 24 months after the award date for aviation maintenance scholarships.

# Information: Hilleman / Morelli Scholarship

MSU is honored to continue the remarkable efforts of Joseph James Legacy Foundation
by awarding the Hilleman/Morelli Scholarship to Montana resident students. This 4-year
scholarship provides a unique blend of financial, academic, leadership, and mentoring
support for students with learning differences.  Hilleman/Morelli scholars will be
selected on their academic, leadership, and career potential.  We seek scholars who
are intrinsically motivated to impact their community with a degree in a science,
technology, engineering or math discipline

If you are ready to roll up your sleeves and get to work, know we are too! To apply
or learn more about this Hilleman/Morelli scholarship, please [visit the Hilleman Scholars Application page for more information](https://www.montana.edu/hillemanscholars/apply.html)

evidence.excerpt:
# Submit an Application

This application is open for students starting at MSU in Fall, 2026!

Scholarship selection is accomplished by a group of dedicated campus partners who
believe in the importance of MSU’s land grant mission. The selection committee are
your partners and champions at MSU, help them make their difficult decision by giving
them a sense of your great potential to lead and your desire to earn a college degree.
Please complete this application with those details in mind. The selection committee
appreciates your honesty, humor, and your aspirations for the future. You are encouraged
to share your application with your guidance counselor, teacher, or coach for review
before submission. The committee is rooting for you! We are excited to receive your
application and learn more about you.

**Please submit the following information for a personal reference.** This may be a high school teacher, coach, counselor, or another significant influence (but not a family member).

Upon submission of your application, a representative from the MSU Hilleman Scholars Program will contact your reference to provide further instruction on completing the recommendation

Essay Question

After reading [Dr. Hilleman's biography](https://www.montana.edu/hillemanscholars/biography.html), please write a brief essay (approximately 500-1000 words) describing how his story inspires your own studies at Montana State University. Please also describe your personal aspirations and how you will channel your work ethic to achieve your academic, leadership, and/or career goals.

evidence.excerpt:
The EAA Ray Aviation Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship program that is funded by the Ray Foundation, managed by EAA, and administered through the EAA Chapters network. Through the generous support of the Ray Foundation, EAA provides up to $12,000 to deserving youths to help cover their flight training expenses, totaling $2,250,000 in annual scholarship funding.

Fund Breakdown

- **Core Scholarship Fund:** All EAA and divisional chapters in the United States and Canada are eligible for a grant up to $12,000.
- **Matching Scholarship Fund:** Chapters that have successfully mentored at least one Ray Scholar through flight training are eligible for a 25/75 matching scholarship. The chapter commits 25% of the award and Ray Foundation will fund the other 75%.

Submission Periods

- **Chapter Applications:** Chapters apply annually from November 1 to January 31 for full $12,000 scholarships, and from November 1 to December 31 for matching scholarships. Chapters that applied for full scholarships are approved by EAA in February. Chapters that applied for a matching scholarship are approved in January.
- **Scholar Applications:** Scholars nominated by chapters with a full scholarship apply from February through August 31 each year. Those receiving a matching scholarship may apply starting in January. Applied scholars are approved by EAA on a monthly basis.

The 2027 chapter application will open on November 1, 2026!

[Ray Aviation Scholarship Chapter Portal](https://webportalapp.com/sp/rayaviationchapter_20)

Important: The portal above is for Ray Aviation Scholarship chapter coordinators only to submit chapter applications and progress reports for their scholars. Scholar candidates, please contact your EAA chapter's scholarship coordinator to learn how to apply for a Ray Aviation Scholarship.

evidence.excerpt:
# Scholar Eligibility and Requirements



Ray Aviation Scholarship recipients are the most engaged, excited, and motivated aspiring pilots that EAA chapters have had the pleasure of meeting. It will be incumbent upon the chapter to vet local youths to help bring forward the most deserving candidate(s) in their local area.

Local candidates must meet the following criteria:

- Age 16-19 to apply for powered flight training (Private or Sport Pilot)
- Age 15-19 to apply for glider training
- Possession of a student pilot certificate (U.S. scholars only)
- Possession of at least a 3rd class medical certificate (Private Pilot students only)
- Received at least one EAA Young Eagles flight
- Able to begin their flight training within 30 days of scholarship start date (the last day of the month in which the scholar was approved by EAA)

Additional consideration will be given to candidates who received multiple Young Eagle flights, are EAA student members, and are actively participating in the EAA Young Eagles Flight Plan, specifically the Sporty’s Learn to Fly Course.

Once selected by the chapter, the candidate will also be screened by EAA through an application process. If approved by EAA, the scholarship recipient must comply with the following requirements:

- Partake in two hours of chapter volunteer service per month, such as:

  - Young Eagles rally volunteering
  - Volunteer at pancake breakfast/fly-ins
  - Chapter aircraft build/restoration project support
  - Chapter gathering participation
  - Chapter newsletter, website, and/or social media maintenance

- Submit regular progress reports during monthly check-ins

- Reach designated flight training milestones, as outlined by EAA's training timeline
  - 3 months to first solo flight (if applicable)
  - 6 months to pass the written exam (if applicable)
  - 12 months to pass the checkride

Important: Funding is dependent upon completion of meeting training milestones and submitting progress reports in a timely manner. Failure to meet milestone deadlines may result in the discontinuance of the award.

The EAA Chapter will play a critical role to ensure the Ray Aviation Scholarship recipient is staying on track to earn their pilot certificate. View the [Chapter Eligibility and Requirements ›](https://www.eaa.org/eaa/eaa-chapters/eaa-chapter-resources/chapter-programs-and-activities/ray-aviation-scholarship-fund/chapter-eligibility-and-requirements)

evidence.excerpt:
The EAA Ray Aviation Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship program that is funded by the Ray Foundation, managed by EAA, and administered through the EAA Chapters network. Through the generous support of the Ray Foundation, EAA provides up to $12,000 to deserving youths to help cover their flight training expenses, totaling $2,250,000 in annual scholarship funding.

Fund Breakdown

- **Core Scholarship Fund:** All EAA and divisional chapters in the United States and Canada are eligible for a grant up to $12,000.
- **Matching Scholarship Fund:** Chapters that have successfully mentored at least one Ray Scholar through flight training are eligible for a 25/75 matching scholarship. The chapter commits 25% of the award and Ray Foundation will fund the other 75%.

Submission Periods

- **Chapter Applications:** Chapters apply annually from November 1 to January 31 for full $12,000 scholarships, and from November 1 to December 31 for matching scholarships. Chapters that applied for full scholarships are approved by EAA in February. Chapters that applied for a matching scholarship are approved in January.
- **Scholar Applications:** Scholars nominated by chapters with a full scholarship apply from February through August 31 each year. Those receiving a matching scholarship may apply starting in January. Applied scholars are approved by EAA on a monthly basis.

The 2027 chapter application will open on November 1, 2026!

[Ray Aviation Scholarship Chapter Portal](https://webportalapp.com/sp/rayaviationchapter_20)

Important: The portal above is for Ray Aviation Scholarship chapter coordinators only to submit chapter applications and progress reports for their scholars. Scholar candidates, please contact your EAA chapter's scholarship coordinator to learn how to apply for a Ray Aviation Scholarship.

# Scholar Eligibility and Requirements



Ray Aviation Scholarship recipients are the most engaged, excited, and motivated aspiring pilots that EAA chapters have had the pleasure of meeting. It will be incumbent upon the chapter to vet local youths to help bring forward the most deserving candidate(s) in their local area.

Local candidates must meet the following criteria:

- Age 16-19 to apply for powered flight training (Private or Sport Pilot)
- Age 15-19 to apply for glider training
- Possession of a student pilot certificate (U.S. scholars only)
- Possession of at least a 3rd class medical certificate (Private Pilot students only)
- Received at least one EAA Young Eagles flight
- Able to begin their flight training within 30 days of scholarship start date (the last day of the month in which the scholar was approved by EAA)

Additional consideration will be given to candidates who received multiple Young Eagle flights, are EAA student members, and are actively participating in the EAA Young Eagles Flight Plan, specifically the Sporty’s Learn to Fly Course.

Once selected by the chapter, the candidate will also be screened by EAA through an application process. If approved by EAA, the scholarship recipient must comply with the following requirements:

- Partake in two hours of chapter volunteer service per month, such as:

  - Young Eagles rally volunteering
  - Volunteer at pancake breakfast/fly-ins
  - Chapter aircraft build/restoration project support
  - Chapter gathering participation
  - Chapter newsletter, website, and/or social media maintenance

- Submit regular progress reports during monthly check-ins

- Reach designated flight training milestones, as outlined by EAA's training timeline
  - 3 months to first solo flight (if applicable)
  - 6 months to pass the written exam (if applicable)
  - 12 months to pass the checkride

Important: Funding is dependent upon completion of meeting training milestones and submitting progress reports in a timely manner. Failure to meet milestone deadlines may result in the discontinuance of the award.

The EAA Chapter will play a critical role to ensure the Ray Aviation Scholarship recipient is staying on track to earn their pilot certificate. View the [Chapter Eligibility and Requirements ›](https://www.eaa.org/eaa/eaa-chapters/eaa-chapter-resources/chapter-programs-and-activities/ray-aviation-scholarship-fund/chapter-eligibility-and-requirements)

evidence.excerpt:
The EAA Ray Aviation Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship program that is funded by the Ray Foundation, managed by EAA, and administered through the EAA Chapters network. Through the generous support of the Ray Foundation, EAA provides up to $12,000 to deserving youths to help cover their flight training expenses, totaling $2,250,000 in annual scholarship funding.

Fund Breakdown

- **Core Scholarship Fund:** All EAA and divisional chapters in the United States and Canada are eligible for a grant up to $12,000.
- **Matching Scholarship Fund:** Chapters that have successfully mentored at least one Ray Scholar through flight training are eligible for a 25/75 matching scholarship. The chapter commits 25% of the award and Ray Foundation will fund the other 75%.

Submission Periods

- **Chapter Applications:** Chapters apply annually from November 1 to January 31 for full $12,000 scholarships, and from November 1 to December 31 for matching scholarships. Chapters that applied for full scholarships are approved by EAA in February. Chapters that applied for a matching scholarship are approved in January.
- **Scholar Applications:** Scholars nominated by chapters with a full scholarship apply from February through August 31 each year. Those receiving a matching scholarship may apply starting in January. Applied scholars are approved by EAA on a monthly basis.

The 2027 chapter application will open on November 1, 2026!

[Ray Aviation Scholarship Chapter Portal](https://webportalapp.com/sp/rayaviationchapter_20)

Important: The portal above is for Ray Aviation Scholarship chapter coordinators only to submit chapter applications and progress reports for their scholars. Scholar candidates, please contact your EAA chapter's scholarship coordinator to learn how to apply for a Ray Aviation Scholarship.
